entities.name: Sieghard von Aquileia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sieghard, also known as Sigehard of Beilstein, served as the influential Patriarch of Aquileia from 1068 until his death on August 12, 1077, during a pivotal period of intense conflict between the Holy Roman Empire and the Papacy. A scion of a prominent Bavarian noble family with extensive estates in Chiemgau, Sieghard's appointment by Emperor Henry IV underscored the imperial strategy of placing loyal, militarily capable figures in key ecclesiastical positions, particularly in strategically vital border regions like northeastern Italy. His tenure was defined by unwavering allegiance to the Emperor amidst the burgeoning Investiture Controversy, positioning Aquileia as a significant imperial bulwark against papal influence and regional rivals.

During his patriarchate, Sieghard was a staunch supporter of Emperor Henry IV, actively participating in imperial diets and military campaigns. He accompanied Henry IV to Worms in 1076, where the Emperor renounced his allegiance to Pope Gregory VII, marking a dramatic escalation of the Investiture Controversy. Sieghard's loyalty was rewarded with significant grants of imperial regalia and territories, including the March of Carniola and the March of Istria in 1077, which dramatically expanded the temporal power and territorial sovereignty of the Patriarchate of Aquileia. This imperial endowment transformed the patriarchate into a powerful prince-bishopric, capable of asserting considerable political and military authority in the region, a status it would largely maintain for centuries.
